page: The Amazon Web Services i4g.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton processor family with Neoverse-N1 cores. The system features 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz with a single execution thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. It provides 512 GB of system memory, matching an 8 GB per core ratio, along with 15,000 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps. Accelerated graphics hardware is absent from this configuration.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput and I/O handling, led by Redis SET performance reaching 72.23 million operations per second and multi-core stress-ng scores placing in the top 25 percent. The instance also delivers high throughput for concurrent compilation tasks and static web serving reaching 45.46 GB/sec, alongside strong small-block cached memory reads of 3784.1 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance shows clear trade-offs, reflected in lower-tier Geekbench single-core scores, single-threaded gzip compression, and sub-optimal token generation throughput across small and large language model inference workloads.

Given its combination of dense NVMe local capacity, high memory allocation, and high-concurrency throughput, the i4g.16xlarge yields strong qualitative hardware efficiency for scale-out, I/O-intensive workloads. It is directly aligned with distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, caching layers, high-throughput search indexing, and real-time log analytics where local NVMe access and parallel core capacity outweigh single-threaded clock speed.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance driven by an arm64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor with 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz. Configured on the Nitro System without hyperthreading, the instance couples 512 GB of RAM with 15,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show upper-quartile parallel throughput in multi-core compute, cached memory access, static web serving, and in-memory key-value processing, reaching 72.23 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core processing and sequential compression tasks show comparatively modest metrics. The balanced memory-to-core allocation and substantial direct-attached storage make the i4g.16xlarge appropriate for distributed databases, high-throughput analytics, and intensive I/O operations.
